newsitem.title: ALBANIA: SOCCER-ALBANIAN TITLE MATCH SUSPENDED AFTER WALKOUT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ALBANIAN TITLE MATCH SUSPENDED AFTER WALKOUT.

text.p: Albania's politically-charged league title decider between Flamurtari of Vlore and Tirana was abandoned 30 minutes from time on Sunday when Flamurtari players walked off in protest against a disallowed penalty.
Tirana, who trailed leaders Flamurtari by two points going into the game, were 1-0 ahead at the time.
The southern port of Vlore was the cradle for violent protests against the Tirana government earlier this year which led to new elections and President Sali Berisha's resignation last month.
The match suspension prompted reaction from both sides with Flamurtari supporters shouting "Vlore, Vlore" and Tirana fans chanting "Down with rebels, down with communists".
Police stepped in as some Flamurtari supporters smashed windows and chairs in Albania's main Qemal Stafa soccer stadium.
There were at least four arrests and Flamurtari players left the stadium under a police escort.

"According to the soccer rules, in such a case it's up to the federation to decide on whether Tirana are the new champions or the match should be played again", said former national striker Shkelqim Muca.

"This is a shameful match and our team have always been discriminated against by the federation," Flamurtari player Ilir Alliu said after his team were forced to return to the field for a while before the match was abandoned.

"I cannot agree with Flamurtari's decision to boycott the match. When we thought we had succeeded in bringing people back to the stadiums, they (Flamurtari) are making them stay away," Tirana official Enver Shehu told state-run television.

The second stage of the 1996-97 Albanian league, which was suspended in February due to armed unrest in the country, resumed 10 days ago in a six-team play-off after the government promised adequate security in stadiums.
